title: Is a Women's Trip to Uganda Right for Your Group? Gorillas, Craft Villages and Slow Days on Lake Bunyonyi
meta_title: Women's Trip to Uganda: Is It Right for Your Group?
meta_description: Plan a women's trip to Uganda for 6 to 12 friends: gorillas, chimps, Lake Bunyonyi, safety, rooming and costs per person. Ask us for a group quote.
excerpt: A women's trip to Uganda for a group of friends: an 8-day route through Kibale, Bwindi and Lake Bunyonyi, with permits, safety, rooming and realistic costs.
content:
A women's trip to Uganda works best as a private group of 6 to 12 friends travelling for about eight days, with chimpanzees in Kibale, a gorilla trek in Bwindi and two unhurried nights on Lake Bunyonyi. You share one guide and vehicle, sleep in small forest lodges and set your own pace.

If you are the one who suggested Uganda, you now carry the permits, the rooms and the worry about whether everyone will cope with a muddy trek. This guide covers the route, safety, costs and rooming from a group leader's view, and shows how our special occasion group safaris handle the paperwork. For the wider picture of the country, start with our Uganda safari tours and destination guide.

Quick Facts

  • Group size: 6 to 12 women fits one or two extended safari vehicles
  • Ideal length: 8 days; 6 at the shortest, 10 to add Murchison Falls
  • Best months: June to September and December to February, the drier spells
  • Gorilla permit: US$800 per foreign non-resident to 31 December 2026 (checked November 2026)
  • Trek group limit: 8 visitors per gorilla family per day, so 12 friends trek in two parties
  • Minimum age: 15 for gorilla trekking
  • Group offer: For every six paying travellers, the seventh place is free

Why Does Uganda Suit a Women's Group?

Uganda suits a women's group because it packs forest walking, great apes, a classic savannah and a calm highland lake into one week, with small lodges where your group fills most of the rooms. The days are active but rarely extreme, so friends with different fitness levels can share almost everything.

The gorilla hour is the heart of a women's trip to Uganda. Bwindi Impenetrable National Park shelters close to half of the world's mountain gorillas, and the trek itself becomes a shared story: the porter who carried someone's bag, the steep slope everyone laughed about at dinner. Our guide to how hard gorilla trekking really is helps you set expectations for the less sporty friends.

Uganda also offers a softer side that many women's groups value: craft villages, coffee and tea country, community walks and evenings without a crowded lodge bar. A women's trip to Uganda can mix two hard-effort days with plenty of slow mornings, which keeps the mood good across a group with mixed ages.

If your group has looked at Rwanda as well, our post on a girls trip to Rwanda covers the shorter, pricier alternative. A women's trip to Uganda usually gives more variety for the money, with longer drives as the trade-off.

What Does an 8-Day Itinerary Look Like?

An 8-day women's trip to Uganda usually runs Entebbe, Kibale, Queen Elizabeth National Park, Bwindi and Lake Bunyonyi, ending with a flight from Kisoro or a road transfer to Kigali. Drive days alternate with walking days so nobody spends two long days in a row on the road.

DayWhereMain activity
1EntebbeArrive at Entebbe International Airport, rest and a welcome dinner
2KibaleDrive west to the crater lakes around Fort Portal, about 5 to 6 hours
3KibaleMorning chimpanzee trek, afternoon Bigodi wetland or crater lake walk
4Queen Elizabeth NPGame drive on the way, afternoon Kazinga Channel boat cruise
5BwindiDrive south, often through the Ishasha sector, about 4 to 5 hours
6BwindiGorilla trek, then a craft or community walk near the lodge
7Lake BunyonyiShort drive to the lake, canoe and island time
8DepartureFly from Kisoro to Entebbe, or drive about 3 to 4 hours to Kigali

Our 7 day Uganda primate and wildlife safari follows the same Kibale, Queen Elizabeth and Bwindi spine, and we can add the Bunyonyi nights for a women's trip to Uganda. Clubs with more time can look at the 9 day Uganda gorilla safari for clubs, which adds rhino tracking and Murchison Falls.

Can a women's trip to Uganda skip the long drives?

Yes. Scheduled light-aircraft flights link Entebbe with airstrips near Bwindi, such as Kisoro and Kihihi, and save most of a day each way. On a women's trip to Uganda, flying works well for the return leg, when everyone is tired, and luggage limits on these small planes mean soft bags rather than hard suitcases.

How Do Gorilla and Chimpanzee Permits Work for a Group?

Each gorilla family in Uganda can be visited by up to 8 people a day, so a group of 9 to 12 women treks with two families at the same time and meets again for lunch. Permits are issued by the Uganda Wildlife Authority, and we book them in one block as soon as your dates are firm.

The gorilla tracking permit costs US$800 per foreign non-resident for treks up to 31 December 2026, and several recent reports say it will rise to US$1,000 from 1 January 2027 (both checked November 2026). Confirm the price for the exact dates of your women's trip to Uganda before you pay deposits, because the rate depends on the trek date.

Chimpanzee tracking in Kibale is listed at US$300 per foreign non-resident from July 2026 (checked November 2026). Our guide to chimpanzee trekking in Kibale explains the morning and afternoon slots, and the group gorilla trekking in Uganda post goes deeper on splitting a large party across families and sectors.

Which sector of Bwindi is best for a women's group?

For a women's trip to Uganda that ends at Lake Bunyonyi, the southern sectors of Rushaga and Nkuringo make the most sense, as they sit about 1.5 to 2 hours by road from the lake. Buhoma in the north is easier to reach from Queen Elizabeth National Park. We match the sector to where permits are free and to the route.

Where Do Crafts, Culture and Lake Bunyonyi Fit In?

The quieter days are where a women's trip to Uganda often comes together. Around Bwindi, village walks lead to homes and workshops where local women weave baskets from grasses and banana fibre, and the money you spend goes straight to the makers. Lake Bunyonyi then gives two nights of canoeing, island visits and long breakfasts.

Lake Bunyonyi sits in the terraced hills near Kabale in southwestern Uganda, dotted with more than twenty small islands. Dugout and fibreglass canoes are the classic way to explore, and lakeside lodges and eco camps suit a group that wants to read, swim off a jetty or walk the ridges without a schedule.

A women's trip to Uganda can also include a coffee or tea walk near Fort Portal, a visit with the Batwa community near Bwindi, or a Kampala craft-market afternoon on the first or last day. We suggest choosing one culture visit per stop so it never feels rushed or staged.

Is Uganda Safe for Women Travelling Together?

A women's trip to Uganda is generally safe on a guided private itinerary, and the main risks are road accidents and petty theft in towns. A private guide-driver, no driving after dark and lodges with staffed grounds remove most of the common worries for a group of friends.

Uganda is a conservative society outside Kampala. Shoulders and knees covered in villages and markets is respectful, and swimwear belongs at the lodge or the lake jetty. Ask before photographing people, especially children, and expect friendly curiosity rather than hassle.

Uganda's laws on same-sex relationships are among the strictest in the world. If anyone in your group is affected, read your government's travel advice carefully before booking. We will always discuss rooming and lodge choice privately and without judgement.

For health planning on a women's trip to Uganda, note that the country removed the yellow fever certificate from its entry requirements in October 2026, yet the vaccine is still recommended for travellers, and malaria is present across the country. Check CDC's yellow fever and malaria guidance by country and see a travel clinic about eight weeks before you fly.

How Much Does a Women's Trip to Uganda Cost?

A women's trip to Uganda of eight days usually costs about US$3,200 to US$7,500 per person sharing, depending on lodge level, group size and whether you fly or drive. The gorilla permit alone is US$800 (checked November 2026), so permits, park fees and the vehicle make up a big share at every level.

TierEstimated cost per person (8 days, sharing)What changes
ComfortableAbout US$3,200 to US$4,200Simple lodges and guesthouses, all road transfers, one gorilla trek
Mid-rangeAbout US$4,200 to US$5,800Well-run forest lodges, a lakeside lodge at Bunyonyi, one flight
UpmarketAbout US$6,000 to US$7,500+Top Bwindi and Kibale lodges, flights both ways, private extras

These estimates for a women's trip to Uganda are built from permit prices and typical lodge rate bands, and they include gorilla and chimpanzee permits. For a published comparison point, our 7 day primate and wildlife trip starts from US$4,537 per adult. The guide to organising a group safari shows how vehicle and guide costs fall per person as your group grows.

How the group pricing works

The vehicle, the guide and the fuel are shared costs, so the price per woman drops as the group fills a vehicle. An extended Land Cruiser with a pop-up roof seats six with a window each; at seven to twelve travellers we use two vehicles and two guides, which also lets the group split for different activities.

For every six paying travellers the seventh place is free. Each woman can pay her own deposit and balance, and friends can arrive on different flights. The tourist eVisa costs US$50 for a single entry and is applied for online through Uganda's official immigration site (checked November 2026), so everyone sorts her own visa.

When Is the Best Time for a Group Trip to Uganda?

The best months for a women's trip to Uganda are June to September and December to February, when forest trails are drier and roads are easier. Gorillas can be tracked all year, so the wetter months of March to May and October to November still work for flexible groups who accept mud and afternoon storms.

Peak months book out first, so a group of ten needing two gorilla families on the same day should hold permits four to six months ahead. In the wetter months lodges are quieter, and the hills around Bunyonyi turn a deep green that photographs beautifully between showers.

Rooming, single rooms and packing

On a women's trip to Uganda most friends share twin rooms, and forest lodges in Bwindi are small, so we confirm the room mix early. Single rooms carry a supplement and may be limited in peak months. Pack layers, gaiters and gardening gloves for the trek; our gorilla trekking packing list has the full kit.

Insider Tips

  • Book permits first: Secure gorilla permits before flights, because a 12-person group needs two families on one day
  • Hire porters: A porter on the gorilla trek supports local families and helps anyone with knees or balance worries
  • One group chat: Share dress guidance, packing and payment deadlines in one place from the start
  • Cash for crafts: Carry small US dollar or Uganda shilling notes for village craft purchases
  • Rest after Bwindi: Plan the lake nights straight after the trek, when legs need a break
  • Insurance: Make sure every policy covers trekking at altitude and medical evacuation

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Uganda safe for a women's group?

Uganda is generally welcoming for a women's group travelling with a private guide, and most visits pass without trouble. The sensible precautions are ordinary ones: no road travel after dark, modest clothing in villages, valuables locked away in Kampala and Entebbe, and a quick read of your own government's travel advice before you book and again before you fly.

How many days does a women's trip to Uganda need?

A women's trip to Uganda needs about eight days to cover chimpanzees in Kibale, a boat cruise in Queen Elizabeth National Park, a gorilla trek in Bwindi and two slow nights on Lake Bunyonyi. Six days works if you skip the savannah, and ten days lets you add Murchison Falls or a second gorilla trek without long driving days.

What does a gorilla permit cost in Uganda?

A gorilla tracking permit in Uganda costs US$800 per foreign non-resident for treks up to 31 December 2026, with reports of a rise to US$1,000 from 1 January 2027 (checked November 2026). Every woman who treks needs her own permit, and permits should be secured four to six months ahead for a group.

Can women in the group pay separately?

Yes. Each traveller can pay her own deposit and balance directly, so the organiser never has to collect money from friends. People can also arrive on different flights, and for every six paying travellers the seventh place is free, which many groups use to cover the organiser or split the saving.

Do we need a yellow fever certificate for Uganda?

Uganda dropped the yellow fever certificate from its entry requirements in October 2026, but the vaccine is still recommended for travellers, and some onward countries may ask for proof if you arrive from Uganda. Speak to a travel clinic about the jab, malaria tablets and routine vaccines about eight weeks before you fly.

Final Thoughts

A women's trip to Uganda rewards groups who plan the permits early and leave room for slow days. Eight days covers chimpanzees, gorillas, a boat cruise and a lake to unwind on, and the shared costs fall nicely once six or more friends sign up.
